algorithm_specification.cost: K formation: (t+1)k A-vector products and tk A^T-vector products. C formation: s additional A^T-vector products. Total (2t+1)k+s, s<=min(n,w). Separately charge dk Gaussian samples, dense rank-revealing orthonormalization O(n*w*min(n,w)), C^T C O(d*s^2), eigendecomposition O(s^3), output O(n*s*k), completion O(n*k^2), and O(n*w+d*s+s^2+dk) storage. Exact fallback: at most d A-vector products, O(n*d*min(n,d)) dense SVD arithmetic and O(nd+nk) storage. A width-k block costs k scalar products. Overall product count O(k log(2d)/sqrt(epsilon)); other resources are not free.
algorithm_specification.query_update_and_output: Draw Pi in R^{d x k} with independent N(0,1) entries. Set B_0=A Pi and B_j=A(A^T B_{j-1}) for j=1,...,t. Retain K=[B_0,...,B_t], w=(t+1)k. Let s=rank(K), Q in R^{n x s} be an exact orthonormal basis. If s>=k, compute C=A^T Q and M=C^T C, order an orthonormal eigenbasis of M by decreasing eigenvalue, and return Z=Q Ubar_k. If s<k, complete Q to k columns by scanning coordinate vectors, discarding zero orthogonal remainders and normalizing nonzero ones. Resolve eigenspace ties using coordinate vectors projected into the tied eigenspace. Exact-SVD output uses the same completion convention.
algorithm_specification.tuning: If d=1 or epsilon<d^(-2), acquire A's d columns if needed, compute its exact SVD and return k orthonormal leading left singular vectors, completing zero singular directions by coordinate Gram-Schmidt. Otherwise set gamma=epsilon/2, L=10^9*d*k^4, p equal to the least positive odd integer at least log2(32*d*(1+L)/epsilon)/(2*sqrt(gamma)), and t=(p-1)/2. Run exactly t updates. No spectral parameter is needed for tuning.

proofs.full_local_argument:
Scope and boundaries. Fix A,n,d,k,epsilon as stated. Put h=min(n,d), r=rank(A), and extend singular values by zero after r. Exact SVD and orthonormal completion give residual sigma_{k+1}, with sigma_{h+1}=0. In the Krylov branch, if r<=k then V_r^T Pi has full row rank almost surely: an r x r Gaussian minor has a nonzero determinant polynomial and hence a measure-zero zero set. Thus range(A Pi)=range(A)=range(K). For r<k, completion contains this range; for r=k, the small eigensolve selects all of it. The residual is zero. This includes A=0, k=r, k>r, k=h and every zero-tail boundary. It remains to consider r>k, so alpha=sigma_{k+1}>0 and rank(K)>=k almost surely.

Gaussian event. In a fixed SVD A=U Sigma V^T, let G=V_k^T Pi, a k x k matrix, and H=V_tail^T Pi, an (r-k) x k matrix, where V_tail contains singular directions k+1,...,r. Their entries are independent standard Gaussians: extend V to an orthogonal basis and apply invariance of the density proportional to exp(-||Pi||_F^2/2). Put a=1/(1000k). Conditional on all other rows of G, their span has dimension k-1 almost surely; the distance of the independent remaining row from that span is |N(0,1)|. Its probability of being below a is at most sqrt(2/pi)*a. By a union bound, all k row distances are at least a except on an event of probability less than 0.001. Column i of G^{-1} is orthogonal to the other rows and has inner product 1 with row i, so its norm is the reciprocal row distance. Hence ||G^{-1}||_2^2<=||G^{-1}||_F^2<=k/a^2=10^6 k^3. Moreover E||H||_F^2=(r-k)k<=dk, so Markov gives P(||H||_F^2>1000dk)<=0.001. With probability at least 0.998 both inequalities hold, and ||H||_2^2||G^{-1}||_2^2<=L=10^9 d k^4.

Filter. Let gamma=epsilon/2 and p,t have the public tuning values. Define T_0(x)=1, T_1(x)=x, T_j(x)=2xT_{j-1}(x)-T_{j-2}(x), and f(x)=(1+gamma)alpha T_p(x/alpha)/T_p(1+gamma). The recurrence yields T_p(cos theta)=cos(p theta), T_p(cosh u)=cosh(pu), and odd parity for odd p. Thus |T_p(x)|<=1 on [-1,1]. For x=cosh u>1, xT'_p(x)/T_p(x)=p coth(u)tanh(pu)>=1 because p>=1 and tanh(pu)>=tanh(u). Therefore T_p(x)/x is nondecreasing for x>1, and f(x)>=x for x>=(1+gamma)alpha. The same recurrence gives T_p(x)=((x+sqrt(x^2-1))^p+(x-sqrt(x^2-1))^p)/2. At x=1+gamma, x+sqrt(x^2-1)>=1+sqrt(gamma). Concavity gives log(1+z)>=z log 2 for 0<=z<=1; hence T_p(1+gamma)>=2^{p sqrt(gamma)-1}. Consequently |f(x)|<=alpha*2^{2-p sqrt(gamma)} for 0<=x<=alpha, using 1+gamma<=2. These conservative constants do not rely on the printed Lemma 5 tail constant.

Sketch residual. Put F=U f(Sigma)V^T, D_1=diag(f(sigma_1),...,f(sigma_k)), D_2=diag(f(sigma_{k+1}),...,f(sigma_r)), and let P project onto range(F Pi). Since f contains only odd monomials of degree at most p=2t+1, F Pi is a linear combination of B_0,...,B_t and lies in range(Q). On the Gaussian event, X=F Pi G^{-1}V_k^T=U_k D_1 V_k^T+U_tail D_2 H G^{-1}V_k^T has columns in range(F Pi). Orthogonality of right singular subspaces gives ||F-X||_F^2=||D_2||_F^2+||D_2 H G^{-1}||_F^2<=(1+L)||D_2||_F^2. Orthogonal projection minimizes columnwise squared error. Therefore ||(I-P)F||_F^2<=(1+L)||D_2||_F^2<=16d(1+L)alpha^2*2^{-2p sqrt(gamma)}<=epsilon alpha^2/2=:eta by the chosen p. This supplies a numerical sketch estimate without importing external Gaussian concentration or the unspecified constant in Lemma 4.

Constrained approximation. Let m count singular values at least (1+gamma)alpha; then 0<=m<=k. If m>=1, ||(I-P)A_m||_F^2=sum_{i<=m}sigma_i^2(1-||P u_i||_2^2)<=sum_{i<=m}f(sigma_i)^2(1-||P u_i||_2^2)<=||(I-P)F||_F^2<=eta. Right-subspace orthogonality gives ||A-P A_m||_F^2=||A-A_m||_F^2+||(I-P)A_m||_F^2. This rank-at-most-m comparator lies in range(Q). For any Y=Q D of rank at most m, Pythagoras gives ||A-Y||_F^2=||(I-QQ^T)A||_F^2+||Q^T A-D||_F^2. A truncated SVD minimizes the latter term: any m-dimensional column subspace captures at most the m largest squared singular values, because its projector has diagonal entries in [0,1] in the left singular basis and their sum is at most m. The first m eigenvectors of M=(Q^T A)(Q^T A)^T give this truncation. Thus B_m=Z_m Z_m^T A satisfies ||A-B_m||_F^2<=||A-A_m||_F^2+eta. Only Property 1's role is needed; Properties 2–3 are not used.

Frobenius-to-spectral implication. For any rank-at-most-m B, sigma_{i+m}(A)<=sigma_i(A-B), 1<=i<=h-m. Indeed, truncate A-B to rank at most i-1, obtaining D with error sigma_i(A-B). Then B+D has rank at most i+m-1, so spectral SVD optimality gives the inequality. That optimality follows because the kernel of any rank-at-most-j matrix intersects the first j+1 right singular directions nontrivially, forcing error at least sigma_{j+1}; truncation attains it. Hence, if ||A-B||_F^2<=sum_{j>m}sigma_j(A)^2+eta, interlacing gives sigma_1(A-B)^2+sum_{j=m+2}^h sigma_j(A)^2<=||A-B||_F^2<=sum_{j=m+1}^h sigma_j(A)^2+eta. Cancel tails to obtain ||A-B||_2^2<=sigma_{m+1}(A)^2+eta. Apply this to B_m. This proves the needed role of Lemma 15 without an unread external Weyl citation.

Corrected constants and nesting. If m=0, contraction gives ||(I-ZZ^T)A||_2<=||A||_2<(1+epsilon/2)alpha<=(1+epsilon)alpha. Otherwise the preceding implication and definition of m give ||A-B_m||_2^2<=((1+epsilon/2)^2+epsilon/2)alpha^2=(1+3epsilon/2+epsilon^2/4)alpha^2<=(1+epsilon)^2 alpha^2, since the difference is epsilon/2+3epsilon^2/4>=0. This keeps the threshold squared instead of adopting equation (13)'s coefficient. Since range(Z_m) is contained in range(Z), (I-ZZ^T)Z_m Z_m^T=0 and (I-ZZ^T)A=(I-ZZ^T)(A-B_m). Orthogonal projection has operator norm at most 1, giving the same final residual bound. This dimensionally valid nesting replaces the printed identity. The Gaussian event has probability at least 0.998, implying the assigned 99/100 guarantee for each fixed input.

Uniform resources and source relation. In the Krylov branch d>=2, k<=d and epsilon>=d^-2, so log2(32d(1+10^9 d k^4)/epsilon)=O(log d) with an absolute constant. Odd rounding adds less than two; thus t=O(log d/sqrt(epsilon)). The filter degree is 2t+1, not the block count. If epsilon<d^-2, then d<epsilon^-1/2, so materializing A for exact SVD uses at most O(k log(2d)/sqrt(epsilon)) scalar products; d=1 is separately exact. This explicitly instantiates the classical partial-SVD alternative mentioned on p.10, rather than attributing a switching rule to the algorithm box. The actual basis dimension is rank(K), not printed qk. Completion, switch and numerical constants are local specifications justified above. The assigned matrix domain, rank domain, epsilon range, relative spectral residual and probability remain unchanged. Arithmetic and storage are separately charged; no unrestricted Oracle Complexity statement follows.
